..
A quiet pattern continues through Friday with little to no light
showers. Friday night, scattered showers and isolated thunderstorms
will be possible for Tinian and Saipan as Invest 99W tracks through
the far northern CNMI, likely between Alamagan and Agrihan. Model
guidance shows 99W slowly strengthening, possibly moving through the
islands as a tropical depression or weak tropical storm. However,
Guam and Rota will likely remain dry with light winds. Breezy
conditions appear unlikely at this time for Tinian and Saipan, and
would be limited to any thunderstorms. Afterwards, periods of
isolated to low end scattered trade wind showers will likely return
for the rest of the forecast period.

Marine...
Light to moderate trade winds are expected before becoming light 
Friday night and then returning Sunday. Combined seas of 6 to 7 ft 
will be steady most of the forecast period. Swells consist of an 
easterly trade wind swell and a small northwest swell. There will be 
a moderate risk of rip currents along north and east facing reefs 
through the weekend. Surf will be elevated along east-facing reefs, 
enhanced by approaching Invest 99W. As 99W passes through the far 
northern CNMI, it may bring scattered showers and isolated 
thunderstorms to the coastal waters of Tinian and Saipan around 
Friday night. Therefore, there will be a moderate risk of lightning 
Friday night near Tinian and Saipan as 99W passes by to the north. 

Tropical Systems...
A weak disturbance, Invest 99W, is found well east of the Marianas,
centered near 16N159E. 99W is moving slowly west-northwest, toward
the northern CNMI. Latest guidance shows 99W moving through near
Alamagan as a weak circulation, developing into a Tropical 
Depression to the west of the islands. However, latest satellite 
data does show a bit more organization with Invest 99W than was
expected. Therefore, developing into a significant tropical cyclone
before reaching the islands is a possibility. Invest 99W will be
monitored closely over the next few days for any indications of 
faster development or change in movement. Residents of the northern 
CNMI should continue to monitor forecasts for any change in expected
movement or intensity. 

For more information on Invest 99W, see bulletins issued by JTWC 
under WMO header ABPW10 PGTW.

Eastern Micronesia...
An overall dry pattern is in place across most of eastern Micronesia
this evening. The only exception is Kosrae. Weak convergence
associated with the Near-Equatorial Trough is generating low-end
scattered showers and isolated thunderstorms that will continue at
Kosrae through tonight, then dry out Friday morning. Otherwise, both
Pohnpei and Kosrae can expect another weak increase in showers over
the weekend, with a 30 percent chance of showers and a slight chance
of thunderstorms Saturday night into Sunday. For Majuro, dry
conditions are expected to continue through the beginning of next
week.

Benign marine conditions are expected to continue through the next
several days, with seas of 3 to 5 feet at Pohnpei and Kosrae, and 4
to 6 feet for Majuro. Light to gentle winds will prevail across the
region.

Western Micronesia...
The monsoon-like pattern remains disorganized and displaced to the
south, with Palau, Yap, and Chuuk all in trade winds. This situation
does not look to change through the entire forecast period, tonight
through Tuesday. After Tuesday, getting toward mid-November, it looks
like the monsoon pattern may start attempting a recovery for one more
big push this year. Often the models are a bit precocious on this
type of thing though, so it could easily bleed over into late
November or even into December.

Meanwhile, Chuuk, Yap, and Palau have primarily isolated showers
through the forecast period. Palau has the most showers with
scattered showers lasting from Sunday through Tuesday, but even here,
QPF is expected to be less than impressive. The good news is, with
winds at or below 15 knots, and seas at or below 5 feet, benign
marine conditions will continue to rule the area.
